caption:
An AI just spent a week almost alone on a physics problem that had stood since 2023.

Claude was handed a nine-loop scattering amplitude in N=4 super Yang-Mills theory — one loop past the record physicist Lance Dixon set in 2023. Dixon checked the answer himself.

→ what a "nine-loop amplitude" actually is
→ how little supervision the run needed
→ who else was racing for the same record
→ why this isn't "AI does physics now"

captions.facebook:
An AI just quietly broke a physics record that had stood since 2023.

Anthropic handed Claude a nine-loop scattering amplitude in N=4 super Yang-Mills theory, a problem one loop past what physicist Lance Dixon solved in 2023. Claude worked almost alone for about a week, running on 96 CPUs, and came back with an answer. Dixon checked it himself and confirmed it held up.

It's not proof that AI can run open-ended research alone, physicists still posed the problem and verified the result. But it's a real step.

slides.title: Claude just broke a physics record that stood since 2023.
slides.sub: A week of near-solo work cracked a problem that had been frontier physics for years.
slides.voiceover: Claude just broke a physics record that had stood since 2023.

slides.label: THE RECORD
slides.title: What Claude actually calculated
items: A nine-loop scattering amplitude in N=4 super Yang-Mills theory
Eight loops, set by physicist Lance Dixon in 2023
Claude Fable 5.1, on Anthropic's Claude Science platform
Lance Dixon himself, independently checking the result
slides.voiceover: It solved a nine-loop amplitude, one loop past the 2023 record.

slides.label: HOW IT RAN
slides.title: Days of work, almost no hand-holding
steps: Anthropic's physicists handed Claude the nine-loop challenge
Claude ran on 96 CPUs, mostly just told to keep going
It tried a direct bootstrap method and an indirect form-factor method
The result went to Lance Dixon, who confirmed it independently
slides.voiceover: It ran for about a week on 96 CPUs, barely supervised, trying two different methods.

slides.label: COST OF A RECORD
slides.title: That's the whole compute bill
slides.sub: A week on 96 CPUs to beat a record that took human physicists years.
slides.voiceover: The whole run cost somewhere between one hundred and two thousand dollars.

slides.label: NOT THE ONLY ONE RACING
slides.title: Two AI-assisted teams, the same weeks
slides.voiceover: A separate team using GPT-6 reached the nine-loop symbol around the same time.

slides.label: READ THE RECORD RIGHT
slides.title: What this isn't
items: N=4 super Yang-Mills isn't real-world particle physics, it's a testbed for methods
Physicists posed the exact problem and checked the final answer
It doesn't mean AI can freely run open-ended research alone
slides.voiceover: It's a toy-model theory, and physicists framed the problem and checked the answer.

slides.title: A week alone
slides.title2: beat a record set by a human physicist.
